_readme: Time-boxed exceptions for scripts/audit-gate.mjs. An entry here suppresses one
advisory in one dependency tree until its expiry date, and not one day longer:
the gate FAILS on a past expiry, it does not warn. Renewal is a commit that
restates the argument, which is the only mechanism that has ever kept an
Every field is required and the gate rejects the file if one is missing.
id            GHSA identifier as it appears in the audit output
tree          one of: pnpm-workspace | site-bubble | discord-bridge
severity      as reported, so a silent escalation is visible in the diff
reason        why the fix is not being taken NOW (usually: it is a major bump)
reachability  why the vulnerable code path is not reachable from shipped code
owner         a person, not a team
expires       YYYY-MM-DD, at most 92 days out
reachability is the field that matters. If you cannot write a specific,
falsifiable sentence there, the honest move is to take the upgrade.

entries.reason: Fix is astro >=5.15.8. apps/web is on astro 4.16.19, so this is a major-version bump that also forces vite 5 -> 6 and touches every page, layout and island in the marketing site. Tracked as its own piece of work rather than smuggled into a security batch.
entries.reachability: Not reachable. The XSS is in the server islands feature, which renders islands per-request on a server. apps/web/astro.config.mjs declares no adapter and no output mode, so the build is static (SSG) and deploys as flat HTML to GitHub Pages. Nothing in apps/web/src uses server:defer, and Astro 4 has no server-islands runtime in a static build to reach.

entries.reason: Fix is astro >=6.3.3, two majors ahead of the installed 4.16.19. Same bump as GHSA-wrwg-2hg8-v723.
entries.reachability: Not reachable. Reflected XSS requires an unescaped slot name derived from a live request. In a static build every slot is resolved at build time from @ff/content, which is our own Supabase-backed copy store, and the output is immutable HTML. There is no request-time rendering path on founderfirst.one for a reflected value to enter.

entries.reason: Fix is astro >=6.4.6, two majors ahead of the installed 4.16.19. Same bump as the two above.
entries.reachability: Not reachable. The SSRF is in the server-side fetch Astro performs for a prerendered error page while handling a request, and it is driven by the Host header. GitHub Pages serves our 404 as a static file; no Astro process handles requests in production, so there is no Host header for Astro to read and no outbound fetch to redirect.

entries.reason: Fix is vite >=6.4.3. Installed is 5.4.21, pinned by astro 4's peer range, so this cannot move until the Astro major lands.
entries.reachability: Not reachable. The bug is a server.fs.deny bypass in the vite DEV server, and only via Windows alternate path syntax. The dev server is never run in production, never bound off localhost, and neither CI (ubuntu-latest) nor the development machines are Windows. Production artifacts are the output of vite build, which does not include the dev server.

entries.reason: apps/web already declares sharp ^0.35.3 directly and resolves 0.35.3, which is patched. The flagged copy is sharp 0.33.5, pinned transitively by astro 4.16.19. It moves when Astro moves.
entries.reachability: Not reachable at runtime. sharp is Astro's build-time image optimiser. It runs on the GitHub-hosted runner, over image files committed to this repository, and produces static assets. No sharp binary is in the deployed artifact and no user-supplied image is ever passed to it. The libvips CVEs need attacker-controlled image input, which would require an attacker to first land a commit.
